title: Cyclic Hom functoriality for canonical total right derivation
statement: Let C and D be Grothendieck abelian categories, F and G additive autoequivalences, and L:C→D additive and left exact, with an equivariance isomorphism e:L⋙G≅F⋙L. Assume the recorded derived categories and K-injective resolutions for C and IsoAlgebra(F). Given a forgetting isomorphism between the canonical total right-derived functors satisfying their unit equation, and natural normalized cyclic boundary families, the induced graded-Hom transport is additive and preserves the cyclic action, native degree-zero morphisms and the degree-minus-one boundary on all bounded native endpoints with bounded derived images. All shifts are the fixed canonical shifts.

proof.text: Use the universal properties to compare the arbitrary-quasi-isomorphism derived functors with the canonical K-injective derived functors by unique unit-preserving natural isomorphisms. Both underlying units commute with shifts; restrict to K-injective objects, where the first unit is invertible, and descend the shift square to show that the underlying comparison commutes with shifts. The canonical-unit shift statement is the already proved private canonical_unit_commShift of CanonicalRightDerivedAdjunctionShift, imported with import all; its statement assumes only an additive functor and K-injective resolutions, not an adjunction.

proof.text: Cancel the exact-localization comparison factors in the assumed exact-square unit equation, yielding the homotopy-category unit equation. Whisker the given canonical forgetting comparison by the native derived comparison and the inverse underlying comparison. Its unit equation and naturality of the underlying comparison identify this with the fixed-pair normalized comparison.

proof.text: Apply cyclicDerivedHom_rightDerived_functorial with boundedness transported along the native comparison. Expand the transported graded Hom map: naturality and shift compatibility cancel the underlying comparison, leaving conjugation by the native comparison. The Frobenius structure is natural in the native endpoints, hence its conjugation action is preserved by these endpoint isomorphisms. The target boundary is natural in both native endpoints, so its square transfers as well. Additivity and degree-zero forgetting follow directly from the same transport formula.

theorem cyclicDerivedCanonicalRight_functorial
    (α : (mapOfNatIso e).rightDerivedFunctor ⋙ (forget G).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      (forget F).mapDerivedCategory ⋙ L.rightDerivedFunctor)
    (hunit : ∀ I : CochainComplex (IsoAlgebra F) ℤ,
      KInjectiveExactSquare.leftUnit (mapOfNatIso e) L (forget F) (forget G) rfl
        (mapOfNatIso e).rightDerivedFunctor (mapOfNatIso e).rightDerivedFunctorUnit I ≫
          α.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj I)) =
      KInjectiveExactSquare.rightUnit L (forget F) L.rightDerivedFunctor
        L.rightDerivedFunctorUnit I)
    (b : CyclicDerivedHomBoundary F) (b' : CyclicDerivedHomBoundary G)
    (hb : CyclicDerivedHomBoundaryNormalized F b)
    (hb' : CyclicDerivedHomBoundaryNormalized G b')
    (hn : CyclicDerivedHomBoundaryNatural F b)
    (hn' : CyclicDerivedHomBoundaryNatural G b')
    : CyclicDerivedHomBoundaryFunctorial F G b b' (mapOfNatIso e).rightDerivedFunctor
        L.rightDerivedFunctor (fun r ↦ L.rightDerivedFunctor.commShiftIso r) α
